data.remark:
Exact (a*b) mod p from three trained ReLU cells on a parallel-prefix pipeline — 100.7 s for the full 1100-case run, T10 at 100%.

Three learned cells (full-adder, full-subtractor, and a scan-combine operator over generate/propagate signals; 8, 8 and 16-row Boolean functions) are the only value-transforming components. Modular addition runs carry and borrow resolution as Hillis-Steele parallel-prefix scans, giving O(log W) depth per modular addition; a fixed Horner double-and-add recurrence over the raw operand bits composes modular additions into the product. The scan topology is fixed routing: which tensors combine at each level is determined a priori by position, never by values.

Official playground: frontier tier T10, overall_accuracy 100% (1000/1000 on tiers 1-10), 100.7 s wall-clock; three revisions of the same weights reproduce identical per-tier counts (100.7 / 103.9 / 105.0 s).

Design note on precision: the cells' complete input space is their truth tables (32 rows total), which makes the bf16 question decidable rather than statistical. Margins were hardened by continued training under a hinge objective to min |logit| >= 6.07, then verified exhaustively at 0 decision flips fp32 vs bf16 with a maximum observed perturbation of 0.09 — a ~65x ratio. Cells therefore run under bf16 autocast with fp32 thresholding, which cut the run from 167 s to ~104 s at no risk to exactness. Randomizing the trained weights collapses accuracy to 0%.
